statement.p: Find the length of the curve x = -\left(3+3t\right),\quad y = -\left(1+4t\right), z = 4-4t, for 4 \le t \le 5.

p.em: (Think of second way that you could calculate this length, too, and see that you get the same result.)

static.solution: \hbox{Length} = \int_4^5 \sqrt{(x'(t))^2 + (y'(t))^2 + (z'(t))^2}\,dt = \int_{4}^{5} \sqrt{(-3)^2+(-4)^2+(-4)^2}\,dt = \sqrt{41}. This is the length of a straight line from the point (-15,-17,-12) to (-18,-21,-16).
